resources.string: Course 7 · The seaside classics: straight lanes, bends, a windmill, a bridge and a sliding gate. One putter, rails that bounce the ball and a 15 cm cup. Bank the ball off the rails, time the moving parts and keep out of the water. 18 short holes.

Course 8 · Nothing here is normal: pipes that swap rooms, black holes, conveyor belts, ice, pinball bumpers, snapping jaws, a spiral and a maze. The same putter and the same rails, on much stranger lanes. 18 holes.

Swipe sideways to aim and pinch to zoom. Draw down anywhere to load the putt: the further you pull, the harder the ball rolls; let go with the needle near the middle. The dashed line shows the path, rails included. Moving obstacles are not in it: time them yourself. The map opens a free aerial view of the whole hole. Water costs a stroke and puts the ball back where you putted from; sand holds it back.

string-array.name: minigolf_tips
string-array.item: A straight lane and a clear line: the best hole to feel how far the putter goes. Aim at the cup and pull until the dashed line reaches it.
Play it in two strokes round the corner, or bank the ball off the far rail: the dashed line shows where it bounces.
The lane bends halfway. Aim at the corner and let the rail send the ball on, or take it in two easy putts.
Two tight turns. Short, controlled putts keep the ball from rebounding off the end of each leg.
Up, across and back down beside the tee. The cup is close to where you started but the way round is long: take it one leg at a time.
Three arms sweep the lane. Wait until a gap opens and roll through it. A soft putt makes you wait longer: a firm one crosses faster.
A hump in the middle: too gentle and the ball rolls back, too hard and it flies past the cup. Look at the dashed line to judge.
A ramp leads to a raised platform. Put enough speed into the putt to climb it, then let the ball run to the cup.
Two bunkers hold the ball back. Go round them through the wide gaps; from sand only a firm putt gets out.
A narrow plank crosses the water. Aim carefully: a ball that falls in costs a stroke and goes back to where you putted from.
Four posts to slalom between. The ball bounces off them: use that to turn the corner of the line.
A gate slides across the lane. Time your putt for when it has opened on one side.
Roll into the pipe and the ball comes out on the far side. You only need to hit the mouth, not to see the cup.
A block stands in the middle of the table. Go round either side or bank the ball off the rails like a billiard shot.
Two ways round the island: the left one is longer but smooth, the right one is short but has a bunker.
A ring round a garden island. A hump on one side, a bunker on the other: choose your side.
Two steps up. Each one slows the ball: give it enough speed for the second step, but not so much that it overshoots the cup.
The grand finish: a gate, a bend, a hump and a moat. Cross the plank, then the cup is just beyond.

string-array.name: minigolf_crazy_tips
string-array.item: Two pipes in the wall of the first room. One leads to the room with the cup, the other sends the ball back to the tee. Choose the right one.
A black hole bends the ball towards it and swallows it if it gets too close. Aim away from it and let it curve your putt in.
Two conveyor belts push the ball sideways, first one way and then the other. Aim so that the second belt brings it back to the middle.
Pinball: bumpers throw the ball back with extra speed. A gentle putt keeps the game under control.
Two windmills turn in opposite directions. Cross the first, then wait for the second.
Three pistons slide at their own pace. Read their rhythm and cross the gaps one at a time.
The whole room is ice: the ball keeps sliding. A gentle push goes a very long way. Bank it off the rails towards the cup.
Mud slows the ball to a crawl; a boost strip throws it forward. Cross the mud with a firm putt and let the strip do the rest.
A spiral lane winds in to the cup at its heart. Cut the corners with the rails and take it in a few strokes.
Three humps, then a funnel round the cup. Keep your speed for the humps: the funnel will guide a slow ball home.
Jaws open and close in front of the cup. Wait for the mouth to open and roll straight through.
A current carries the ball towards a waterfall on the right. Aim to the left and let the stream bring you back.
One planet pulls the ball in, the other pushes it away. Let them bend your putt, and keep clear of the one that swallows.
The floor tilts: the ball drifts sideways. Aim uphill and let the slope bring it back to the cup.
Propellers fill the room. Slip past them one at a time.
The tee stands high: the ball picks up speed on the slide by itself. A very gentle push is enough, and sand waits behind the cup.
A small maze with dead ends. Find the way through, and use the rails to turn the corners.
Everything at once: a windmill, a belt and a pipe, then a black hole, a bunker and the cup. Take your time.
